basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 8.' and it opens 'Vers. 8. Fecit grande convivium. Juxta litteram convenientius fuit ut in die nativitatis'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 8. Fecit grande convivium. Juxta litteram convenientius fuit ut in die nativitatis vel circumcisionis ejus Abraham epulum faceret. Sed vir prophetico plenus spiritu hoc in die ablactationis facere maluit. Significabatur enim per hoc, qua tunc Deo et angelis festivitatem quodammodo facimus quando lacte infantiae dimisso in virum perfectum evadimus et solido jam cibo utimur.
